title: What is known about 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_0LE1LD_0RE1LF_---1LA_1LD0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_0LE1LD_0RE1LF_---1LA_1LD0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the left-going pass and its endings by block length mod 3, including the halting one (a leftmost block of length 3n+3), and the counter configuration at step 235,323. That halting needs the left end rests on the observation that inside the tape 0s are single. The macro simulator finds no halt in 1016 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 45,452 cells have been visited and 41,814 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474).

claims.title: The halting patterns
claims.text: 0 C> 0 and D> 0 0 halt (E reads 0), and by the table these are the only ways: both need two adjacent 0s.

claims.title: The pass and its endings
claims.text: C, D, F walk left turning 111 into 011 (pass); a block of length 3n+1 stops the pass (stop_1), one of length 3n+2 is crossed (cont_2), one of length 3n+3 stops it (stop_3) or, if it is the leftmost block, halts the machine (halt_3). For all n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The counter at step 235,323
claims.text: After 235,323 steps the tape is Q (01)^333 with the head in state A on a final 1 (Q a fixed 84-cell prefix).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>16</sup> steps; the depth front
claims.text: The macro simulator finds no halt and no new leftmost cell after step 234,511; the deepest pass reached 44 cells from the left end at 2.5·10<sup>11</sup> steps and went no deeper up to 10<sup>16</sup>.

claims.title: Halting needs the left end
claims.text: At every excursion start in the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps the 0s inside the tape are single, so the halting patterns can only form at the leftmost block.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: it halts iff a pass ends on the leftmost block while its length is a multiple of 3. The leftmost block is 1 1 now.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Each time the head comes back from the right end it walks left rewriting the 1s three at a time, and stops at the first block whose length is not 2 more than a multiple of 3. The machine halts only if it stops on the very first block of the tape and that block's length is a multiple of 3.

facts.text: The way to halt: a pass ends on a leftmost block of length 3n+3.
The counter on the tape at step 235,323, proved in Lean.
No halt; the deepest pass is 44 cells from the left end.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474).
After 109 steps the tape spans 45,452 cells (9 left of the start, 33,486 right), with a density of 1s of 0.92.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The pass, by length mod 3
html: The tape is a row of blocks of 1s with single 0s between them. Each time the head comes back from the right end it walks left in states C, D, F, writing a 0 into every third cell. What happens at the next separator depends on the length of the block it has just crossed:

block lengthwhat happenstheorem
3n+1the head turns rightstop_1
3n+2the pass goes on into the next blockcont_2
3n+3the head turns rightstop_3
3n+3, first block of the tapeE reads 0: halthalt_3
Then it sweeps back right, flipping pairs 11 ↔ 01. All of these are Lean theorems for every n and every tape around them.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is E on 0, reached from C on 0 moving left or D on 0 moving right: both need two 0s side by side. Inside the tape the 0s are single (observed, not proved), so the pattern can only form against the blank tape on the left, when a pass ends on the first block and that block has a length divisible by 3.

sections.heading: A counter that creeps left
html: At step 235,323 the tape is a fixed 84-cell prefix followed by 333 blocks of length 1 (proved in Lean, counter_start). Blocks of length 1 stop passes, so most passes are shallow; now and then one reaches far left, and the deepest so far moves slowly:

depth from the left endright-end recordsstep
742,2417.3·106
6632,0512.0·109
64179,3156.4·1010
44356,4112.5·1011
(none deeper)to 1016

The first block is 1 1, which passes cross, so reaching it now gives a new leftmost cell rather than a halt. Starting from other counter lengths m the front reaches the left end without a halt for m = 6 … 10, 32 and 39, and takes more than 1015 steps for the other m ≤ 40: no clean law in m was found.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html: Proved in Lean by the kernel: the halting patterns and the pass with all its endings. With native_decide: the counter at step 235,323. Measured with a simulator: no halt in 1016 steps, the depth records, the small-counter runs. Not proved: that the 0s inside the tape stay single, a macro step on the word of block lengths, and anything about the first block when the front arrives.

family: Mod-3 pass counter: a pass ends at the first block of length 0 or 1 mod 3; halting needs a leftmost block of length 3n+3
summary: Every excursion sends a pass left that rewrites 1s three at a time and ends at the first block of length ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 3); the machine halts only if a pass ends on the leftmost block when its length is a multiple of 3. The deepest passes creep towards the left end like a counter; no halt in 10^16 steps.
